_comment: C0-8 正文英译 · github-mcp（2026-10-25）。官方英文引文原样保留（B 类）。

axes.model_access:
**It calls no model itself.** It is an interface implementation called by clients — **which model to pick is the client's business.**

It wraps GitHub platform capabilities as MCP tools: repositories, issues, PRs, Actions, code scanning, etc.
Two details:

- Tool schemas return typed `structuredContent` on protocol version `2026-07-28` and later;
  older clients fall back to plain text

- Tool descriptions can be overridden via `github-mcp-server-config.json` or `GITHUB_MCP_*` environment variables (useful for localization)
axes.runtime:
**Two run forms: remotely hosted, or a local process.**

**Remote hosting** is operated by GitHub itself, endpoint `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`.

**The local form** runs three ways:

- Docker image `ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server`
- A `go build` binary
- Its built-in HTTP mode `github-mcp-server http` (default port 8082)

⚠ **GitHub Enterprise Server does not support remote hosting** (stated explicitly by the official docs). Only the local form works.
`ghe.com` can use remote hosting, but on a separate endpoint.

**The official wording on the remote form**: "the easiest method for getting up and running"
"no local setup or runtime required"
axes.local_files:
**It never touches your local file system.**

It operates on the GitHub platform: remote repositories, issues, PRs. It has no direct relation to your local git repositories.
For local git operations see this site's git entry.

The only capability close to "files" is **operating on remote repository content**:

- `get_file_contents` — read a file or directory
- `create_or_update_file` / `push_files` — write files
- `delete_file` — delete a file

The scope is repos/branches on GitHub. **The container form needs no local repository mount either.**
axes.background:
**The remotely hosted form is independent of your client process.** The service lives on GitHub's side; it stays online when you shut down.

**The local form lives and dies with the client** — the stdio child process stops on exit.
The self-hosted HTTP mode is a resident service you operate yourself, i.e. `github-mcp-server http` behind a reverse proxy.

⚠ **It offers no "background task resumption" semantics.** Its modes are stateful HTTP / stdio sessions;
there is no official checkpoint-resume mechanism. "Always on" refers to the availability of the remotely hosted form —
and that availability depends on GitHub's service status.
axes.tools:
**Toolsets are the core mechanism of this entry.**

Narrowing capability has four layers of control:

- `--toolsets` / `GITHUB_TOOLSETS` (remote: the `X-MCP-Toolsets` header, or the `/x/{toolset}` path)
- `--tools` / `GITHUB_TOOLS` — down to the individual tool
- `--exclude-tools` — exclude tools
- In the remote form each toolset has its own URL, easy to combine per scenario

**The default toolsets** are 5 groups: context · repos · issues · pull_requests · users.

Another 20+ groups can be enabled: actions · code_security · dependabot · discussions · gists · git ·
governance · labels · notifications · orgs · projects · secret_protection ·
security_advisories · stargazers · code_quality · copilot, etc.

The remote form also has exclusive toolsets, e.g. Copilot Spaces and GitHub Support Docs Search.
axes.context:
**No cross-session memory.** Each session is independent. State lives on the GitHub platform itself
(persistent state of repos, issues, PRs), not in the server.

One official-specific context control exists. In Insiders mode `list_*` tools can return CSV
(the `csv_output` feature flag), used to compress list-type responses.

⚠ **That is a response-format optimization, not a memory mechanism.**

**The official wording**: "reduce response context for agents"

The README provides no built-in memory or retrieval layer.
axes.permissions:
**Permissions are determined by the GitHub token; the official docs add three narrowing controls.**

- **① read-only mode** — `--read-only` / `GITHUB_READ_ONLY` / `X-MCP-Readonly`
- **② lockdown mode** — `--lockdown-mode` / `X-MCP-Lockdown`
- **③ scope filtering** — classic PATs hide tools the token lacks at startup;
  OAuth uses on-demand scope challenges

read-only is **an enforced filter with the highest precedence**: even if you explicitly request write tools, they get disabled.

⚠ **lockdown is not an authorization boundary.** The official docs state it is only a best-effort content filter
(filtering content produced by users without push access in public repositories);
**it does not change what the underlying credential can read or write**.

**Write and delete capabilities are complete**: create / update / delete file, `push_files`,
`merge_pull_request`, `create_repository`, `delete_repository`, etc.
High-risk tools require on-demand authorization (e.g. the `delete_repo` scope).

The official docs call read-only a **"strict security filter"**
axes.fit:
**In one sentence: it lets any MCP client operate GitHub in natural language.**

Clients include VS Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Codex, Gemini CLI, etc.
What it can do: read code and repository structure, manage issues and PRs, monitor Actions.
It can also check code scanning / dependabot security alerts and read notifications.

**The remotely hosted form suits people who do not want to operate it themselves.**
**The local Docker form suits**: GitHub Enterprise Server users · people who need self-hosted HTTP ·
people who want offline control.

**Not a fit** for two kinds of scenarios. First, operating the local file system — that is the filesystem / git server's job.
Second, scenarios needing cross-session memory.

mcp.transport:
**Two forms: local stdio, or remotely hosted HTTP.**

The local form uses **stdio**, two ways to run: the Docker image
`ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server`, or the `github-mcp-server stdio` binary.

The remotely hosted form uses **Streamable HTTP**, endpoint `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/`.

You can also self-host the HTTP mode (`github-mcp-server http`), with OAuth metadata endpoints and scope challenges.

The remote form accepts URL path modifiers:

- `/readonly` — read-only
- `/insiders` — insider features
- `/x/{toolset}` — expose only one toolset
- These can be combined

**⚠ The permission boundary differs between forms and must be configured separately.**

**Verified against**: the official README and remote-server.md (2026-10-08)
mcp.auth:
**Local stdio has three authentication methods.**

- **Browser OAuth** — on github.com the official mirror ships app credentials; the token is kept in memory only
- **PAT** — environment variable `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN`, **takes precedence over OAuth**
- **GitHub App** — for non-interactive stdio

**Remote hosting** has two: OAuth (using GitHub credentials, with on-demand scope challenges when a scope is missing),
or a PAT (the `Authorization: Bearer` header).

⚠ **An easy trap: the two PAT kinds behave differently.**

- **Fine-grained PATs (`github_pat_`) do no scope filtering** — all tools are shown,
  permissions are enforced API-side

- Only **classic PATs (`ghp_`)** hide tools by scope at startup

GitHub Enterprise Server / ghe.com require your own OAuth App or GitHub App.
mcp.scope:
**The scope is the permission range of the GitHub token — it can read, and also write and delete.**

Three layers can narrow it: **read-only mode** enforces read-only (highest precedence) ·
**toolsets trimming** shrinks the exposed surface · **lockdown mode** filters untrusted content
(⚠ the official docs stress it is **not an authorization boundary**).

**Write / delete capabilities are complete**, for example:

- Files: `create_or_update_file` / `push_files` / `delete_file`
- Repositories: `create_repository` / `delete_repository` (requires `delete_repo`)
- PRs: `create_pull_request` / `merge_pull_request`
- Others: `label_write` / `projects_write` / `create_repository_ruleset`

**There is no independent approval mechanism.** `delete_repository` goes through multi-round confirmation,
but that is interactive elicitation, not an approval layer — do not treat it as one.

sections.⚠ 先澄清一个最容易搞混的点:
It is **not** the archived reference server from the MCP organization. The original `github` reference server was archived to
[servers-archived](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers-archived/tree/main/src/github),
while this entry refers to **GitHub's own repository `github/github-mcp-server`** —
actively maintained (rolling re-check 2026-10-23: latest release v2.0.3 @ 2026-10-21), MIT, 33k+ stars.

> The reason for fixing this entry is direct: the two entries share a name, and searching "github mcp server" hits both
> "the archived reference implementation" and "GitHub's official active product", whose capabilities and maintenance status are completely different.
sections.两种形态:
| | **Remotely hosted** | **Local** |
|---|---|---|
| Endpoint / command | `https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/` | Docker `ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server` / `github-mcp-server stdio` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP | stdio |
| Who operates it | GitHub | You |
| Authentication | OAuth / PAT | OAuth (browser, token in memory only) / PAT |
| Prerequisite | The client supports remote MCP | Docker or the Go binary |
| GHES | **Not supported** | Supported (`--gh-host` / `GITHUB_HOST`) |

The official positioning of the remote form, original wording: **"the easiest method for getting up and running"**,
**"no local setup or runtime required"**; the local form is the fallback for clients that do not support remote MCP / for GHES.
sections.Toolsets：本 server 最值得讲的设计:
**Only 5 groups load by default** (context / repos / issues / pull_requests / users);
the rest must be enabled explicitly — the official rationale is "helping LLMs choose tools and reducing context". The configuration quartet:

- `--toolsets` / `GITHUB_TOOLSETS` (remote: the `X-MCP-Toolsets` header or the `/x/{toolset}` URL)
- `--tools` / `GITHUB_TOOLS` (down to the individual tool)
- `--exclude-tools` / `GITHUB_EXCLUDE_TOOLS` (exclusions; takes precedence over the previous two)
- The special value `all` enables every toolset

**Remote and local toolsets are not identical**: remote additionally has Copilot Spaces and GitHub Support Docs Search,
plus the `create_pull_request_with_copilot` tool that invokes the Copilot coding agent.
sections.read-only 与 lockdown：两个容易高估的开关:
| Mode | Switch | Official characterization |
|---|---|---|
| **read-only** | `--read-only` / `X-MCP-Readonly` | **strict security filter**, highest precedence; explicitly requested write tools still get disabled |
| **lockdown** | `--lockdown-mode` / `X-MCP-Lockdown` | **best-effort content filter, not an authorization boundary** |

The official docs are concrete about lockdown's boundary. It reduces exactly one prompt-injection risk:
**content produced by users without push access in public repositories**.
It **does not change what the underlying credential can read or write**. Content hidden from filtered responses
may still be reachable through other tools, or by calling the GitHub API directly
(`github-actions[bot]` and `copilot` are exceptions, always treated as trusted).
sections.认证与权限：token 决定一切:
- **Classic PAT (`ghp_`)**: at startup, tools the token lacks are **hidden** based on `X-OAuth-Scopes`.
- **OAuth (remote)**: no pre-hiding; instead a **scope challenge** — when a tool missing a scope is used, authorization is requested on demand.
- **Fine-grained PAT (`github_pat_`) / GitHub App**: **no tool filtering**; everything is shown; permissions are enforced by the GitHub API side.

The official credential best practices: minimal scopes (`repo` / `read:packages` / `read:org`), separate tokens per environment,
regular rotation, no hardcoding. Some hosts such as Windsurf can only hardcode, and the official docs call out that exception too.
sections.核验说明:
The basis for `confidence: partial` (2026-10-08):

All eight dimensions and the three mcp dimensions carry conclusions, but in two places
**the official docs themselves have no content**, leaving only "not stated officially":
so-called "dynamic tool discovery" cannot be found in current official docs (see unknowns). The official docs also provide no tool-level approval mechanism.
These are not evidence gaps but things the official side currently does not provide, which is why it cannot be raised to verified.

**Official pages verified this round**: README (two forms, the full toolsets table, authentication, read-only / lockdown, i18n overrides),
docs/remote-server.md (endpoint, URL modifiers, X-MCP-* headers), docs/server-configuration.md,
docs/scope-filtering.md, docs/streamable-http.md, docs/insiders-features.md, docs/feature-flags.md;
repository metadata verified via the GitHub API (33,871★, MIT, Go, last push 2026-10-22, latest release v2.0.3; rolling re-check 2026-10-23).

This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/mcp/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/mcp/_protocol.md).

**Suggested measurement**: the focus for this server is "can it be reined in" —

| # | What to test | Why it is worth testing |
|:--:|---|---|
| 1 | With only the `repos` toolset + read-only, are write tools really disabled | The official docs claim read-only has the highest precedence; needs verification |
| 2 | Under lockdown, is content from unauthorized users' issues really filtered | The official docs already say it is not a security boundary; verify its actual strength |
| 3 | Tool-visibility differences between classic PAT vs fine-grained PAT | The official docs say fine-grained PATs do no scope filtering — easily misread as "identical permissions" |
| 4 | Toolset differences between remote hosting and local Docker (Copilot-exclusive tools) | The two forms expose different tool surfaces; confirm before choosing |
| 5 | Prerequisites of `delete_repository`'s multi-round confirmation in HTTP mode | Requires `GITHUB_MCP_SERVER_MRTR_STATE_KEY` to be configured, otherwise the tool is not exposed |
unknowns:
- The "dynamic tool discovery" capability (a `--dynamic-toolsets` kind of thing): **not stated in the current official README or docs** (checked seven pages: README, server-configuration.md, remote-server.md, insiders-features.md, feature-flags.md, streamable-http.md, scope-filtering.md); the only runtime-adjustable mechanisms are Feature Flags (`--features` / `X-MCP-Features`) and Insiders mode
- A tool-level human approval mechanism (not stated officially; the official docs offer only three narrowing controls: read-only / lockdown / OAuth challenges)
- SLA / rate-limit details of the hosted form (neither README nor remote-server.md gives numbers)
- The complete lockdown filtering matrix across tools (the official docs list only a few branches under issue_read / pull_request_read)
- Quota and operational details of the self-hosted HTTP mode behind a reverse proxy (the official docs give config knobs, no capacity numbers)
related: **The entry to contrast most**: the git server does **local** repository operations only, with no push/PR, and explicitly notes the original github reference server is archived; this entry is precisely the official replacement for that "remote GitHub operations" role.
Scope/permission-design contrast: filesystem is a local directory allowlist; github-mcp is a remote GitHub token scope.
Same-kind contrast: Context7 is purely remotely hosted with no local permission risk; github-mcp is a "local + remote" dual form with full write/delete capability.
